title: Jump Game IX
summary: Given an integer array nums, for each index i, find the highest value in nums that can be reached by following a sequence of valid jumps.
statement: Given an integer array nums, for each index i, find the highest value in nums that can be reached by following a sequence of valid jumps. A jump to a higher index j (where j > i) is valid only if nums[j] nums[i]. The result is an array ans where ans[i] is the highest value reachable starting from index i.
constraints: Jump right only to a smaller value or left only to a larger value.
Return the maximum value reachable from every start.
hints: A suffix value below the current prefix maximum connects the current region to the already-solved region on its right.
Compute prefix maxima, then scan backward with the suffix minimum.
If prefix_max exceeds the later suffix minimum, copy the next answer; otherwise close a region at prefix_max.
The strict crossing supplies jumps in both directions between regions, while absence of a crossing makes the current prefix maximum the greatest reachable value.
editorial: The strict crossing supplies jumps in both directions between regions, while absence of a crossing makes the current prefix maximum the greatest reachable value.

tests.explanation: The first two indices share maximum reachable value two; the last remains three.
Every index can reach the value three through valid jumps.
